page.title: Style Library
page.purpose: Let an operator find, read, compose, and version a writing voice, and see plainly whether a style is owned by a file in another scenario or authored here.

priorities.statement: Whether this style is file-owned or operator-authored, before any edit is attempted
What this style actually instructs, resolved rather than as fragments
Which version is frozen because something shipped against it

elements.name: Styles
elements.description: All registered styles with provenance and status.

elements.name: Authority
elements.description: Declared-by-consumer or operator-authored. Determines whether editing is possible at all.

elements.name: Resolved style
elements.description: The fully merged effective style, including everything inherited through extends.

elements.name: Conformance
elements.description: Targets met or missed and anti-pattern hits located by span.

elements.name: Edit
elements.description: Unavailable for a declared style, stating the owning file path.

elements.name: Export for commit
elements.description: One-way export of an operator-authored style to declaration file content.

states.description: A file-owned style: editing is unavailable and the owning path is named.
An operator-authored style under the reserved local namespace; editable and exportable.
A version referenced by a committed output; mutation refused with a create-new-version affordance.
Merged targets have an empty intersection; both contributing versions and the conflicting metric are named.
The owning declaration file was deleted; the style is retained for provenance and refuses new generation.
Data for this surface is in flight; skeleton structure is shown rather than a blank frame.
Some data resolved and some did not; what resolved stays usable and what failed is named rather than silently omitted.
Displayed data is known to be out of date relative to its source; the surface says so rather than presenting it as current.
The request failed; the specific cause is stated inline and the surface offers the action that retries it.

claims.statement: A style's authority is visible on the style itself before any edit is attempted.
claims.rationale: Discovering that a record is file-owned only by being refused is a worse experience than being told up front. (Tier: aspirational until the UI exists and accessibility captures can join these bindings; promote to machine at that point — the binding testids above are the contract the UI must satisfy.)

claims.statement: A declared style offers Export for commit and never offers Save.
claims.rationale: The file is the source of truth. A Save affordance would imply a round-trip sync that deliberately does not exist. (Tier: aspirational until the UI exists and accessibility captures can join these bindings; promote to machine at that point — the binding testids above are the contract the UI must satisfy.)

claims.statement: A resolution conflict names both contributing versions and the conflicting metric.
claims.rationale: A conflict that only says it failed is not actionable when styles compose through extends. (Tier: aspirational until the UI exists and accessibility captures can join these bindings; promote to machine at that point — the binding testids above are the contract the UI must satisfy.)

claims.statement: A frozen version is perceivably distinct and states that a committed output references it.
claims.rationale: Immutability that looks like a bug erodes trust in the whole versioning model. (Tier: aspirational until the UI exists and accessibility captures can join these bindings; promote to machine at that point — the binding testids above are the contract the UI must satisfy.)
